name: Urban Historic Centre of Cienfuegos
description: Cienfuegos is a Caribbean port city on Cuba's south-central coast, founded in 1819 by settlers of mostly French origin. Its tidy grid of streets is lined with neoclassical and later eclectic buildings, including the Government Palace, the Ferrer Palace and the old lyceum. Built on sugar, tobacco and coffee trade, it was among the first Latin American towns laid out around ideas of order and hygiene.
